question: Does hiring an agent on your marketplace beat doing the job yourself, and can you prove it?

venues: two venues: a one-way venue (synthetic) vs a balanced venue (synthetic)

tasks.task: Earn — fees on a liquidity position
tasks.metric: net return on capital (fees − realized convexity cost − costs), P25–P75
tasks.without_agent: mint once at the same width, never touch it (passive_policy)
tasks.note: baseline: 0 usable replays, assumption A5 requires 20; 60 window(s) were shorter than the 24h policy horizon; agent: 0 usable replays, assumption A5 requires 20; 60 window(s) were shorter than the 24h policy horizon

attention.note: Counted, not timed. The DIY column's moves are decisions somebody had to make; the agent's are decisions it made instead, at times its policy chose rather than times anyone was watching. Turning either into hours would need a minutes-per-decision assumption this report does not have.

hire_cost.note: 0.000755 BNB — the keystore's own registration fee (0.000724, read from getRegistrationFeeInWei on chain 56) plus 0.000031 of gas for the grant and revoke, measured from the recorded round trip. One hire, one expiry.

you_also_pay.note: The strategy's own gas and slippage while the task runs, which is a different quantity from the fee to hire and is charged to both columns by the same cost model.

tasks.verdict: no verdict — baseline: 0 usable replays, assumption A5 requires 20; 60 window(s) were shorter than the 24h policy horizon; agent: 0 usable replays, assumption A5 requires 20; 60 window(s) were shorter than the 24h policy horizon
